analysis_status: post-result same-site same-week robustness on a detection-sensitive binary-link response; not confirmatory or effort-standardized

all_annual_2006_2011.exception_context: The broad sensitivity includes the known expanded 2006 site pool; both endpoints have negative held-out log-loss skill for this transition.

ecological_read.supported: The repaired current-state opportunity signal persists when focal-plant flowering and focal-pollinator activity on other plants must coincide within the same site and ISO week. It is therefore not generated solely by pooling spatially separated observations within a week.
ecological_read.formation: In the strict-core scope, previously absent dyads with positive same-site same-week focal-excluded opportunity form links at 12.72% versus 2.96% when opportunity is zero (rate ratio about 4.29).
ecological_read.persistence: Among established links, loss occurs at 47.14% with positive same-site same-week opportunity versus 61.74% when opportunity is zero.
ecological_read.scope: These are contemporaneous observational associations measured through the same field sampling process.
ecological_read.current_interpretation: Same-site same-week matching shows the binary association is not solely caused by pooling spatially separated observations, but the later census-effort audit shows the binary response remains materially detection-sensitive.

not_established: causal effect of local spatiotemporal co-occurrence
strict future-link forecasting from past-only data
true absence for zero observed links
claim_ceiling: Post-result spatiotemporal robustness of a detection-sensitive binary association only. Same-site same-week persistence does not establish causality, sampling-effort independence, strict forecasting, ecological rewiring, decision equivalence, or routeability; the effort-standardized census-incidence opportunity increment is fold-mixed.

supersession.interpretation: retain as spatiotemporal robustness of a detection-sensitive binary association, not as an effort-independent mechanism
